negative_findings.description: No publicly indexed bank-level credit rating reports were found for standalone Montenegrin banks (Hipotekarna banka, Universal Capital Bank, Lovcen banka, Adriatic Bank) from Fitch, Moody's or S&P.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two separate searches returned only sovereign ratings for Montenegro and parent-group ratings (Erste, OTP); no Montenegro-domiciled bank issuer rating pages surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The premise that rating agencies profile Montenegrin bank management may hold only indirectly, via parent-group reports; A5 leadership signals must lean on IFI and issuer disclosure instead.

negative_findings.description: Rating-agency primary sites (Fitch, Moody's, S&P) and Cbonds require accounts for the substantive commentary.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only aggregator mirrors (countryeconomy, tradingeconomics, FX Empire) were freely visible; those carry ratings but no management commentary.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any workflow depending on agency prose about bank management needs a licence; free aggregators cannot substitute.

brief: For Montenegro's jobs/leadership/organisation signals, the international English-language layer is dominated by three reliable pillars: EBRD (a large, well-documented Montenegro portfolio whose project summary documents exist in Montenegrin as well as English, and whose signing press releases name bank management-board chairs by name), the IMF Article IV cycle (which speaks explicitly to whether the CBCG is operationally independent and 'appropriately staffed'), and the EU accession machinery (the annual Commission country report SWD, the European Parliament rapporteur report, and Montenegro's own bilingual eu.me Chapter 9 pages), supplemented by CBCG's twinning/IPA project pages and the partner central banks — HNB, Bundesbank, BaFin, DNB — that publish their own accounts of CBCG organisational reform. The rating-agency premise is the weakest leg of this cell: no bank-level ratings for Montenegro-domiciled banks surfaced, and agency commentary sits behind registration, so ownership and management change is better tracked through issuer disclosure at parent level — currently the Addiko/RBI/NLB contest and the planned carve-out of Addiko's Montenegrin unit. Local-language material is present and productive (EBRD's Montenegrin PSDs, MINA, Bankar.me's EBRD tag stream) but under-sampled here because the session's search budget was exhausted after one sr query. The clearest remaining gaps are the IFI recruitment/tender channels (the most literal 'jobs' evidence in this cell), WBIF/EIB, and foreign wires such as bne IntelliNews.
